pageInfo.subtitle: Master the art of smooth, connected playing through hammer-ons, pull-offs, and advanced legato combinations.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Legato playing creates smooth, flowing musical lines by connecting notes seamlessly through hammer-ons, pull-offs, and slides. This essential technique allows for expressive phrasing, increased speed with less picking, and the ability to create vocal-like melodic passages that sing with emotion and fluidity.

items.text: Strike the fret firmly with fingertip
Keep unused fingers close to fretboard
Pre-fret the lower note before pull-off

exercises.title: Basic Hammer-Ons
exercises.description: Start with simple two-note hammer-ons to develop the fundamental motion. Focus on generating clear, even volume from the fretting hand alone.

patternNote.text: Technique: Pick the first note, then hammer the second note with your fretting finger

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Strike the fret firmly with your fingertip, not the pad. The hammered note should be as loud as the picked note. Practice on all strings to develop consistent technique.

exercises.title: Basic Pull-Offs
exercises.description: Develop smooth pull-off technique by learning to "pluck" the string with your fretting finger while revealing the lower fretted note underneath.

patternNote.text: Technique: Pre-fret both notes, pick the higher note, then pull off to the lower note

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Before picking, make sure both fingers are properly positioned. The pull-off motion should be quick and decisive, moving perpendicular to the string.

exercises.title: Hammer-On + Pull-Off Combinations
exercises.description: Combine hammer-ons and pull-offs to create flowing three-note patterns. This forms the foundation for more complex legato passages.

patternNote.text: Pattern: Pick - Hammer - Pull-Off (only one pick attack per group)

notation.title: Three-Note Legato Groups on All Strings

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Each three-note group should be completely smooth and connected. Focus on maintaining consistent volume and timing throughout the legato passage.

exercises.title: Four-Note Legato Patterns
exercises.description: Extend your legato technique to four-note patterns using combinations of hammer-ons and pull-offs. This develops finger independence and stamina.

patternNote.text: Pattern: Pick - Hammer - Hammer - Pull-Off variations

notation.title: Four-Note Legato Groups: Ascending and Descending

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Keep all four fingers close to the fretboard and pre-positioned. The third finger must be strong enough to generate a clear hammered note on the highest fret.

exercises.title: Scale-Based Legato Playing
exercises.description: Apply legato technique to musical scales, creating smooth, flowing lines that sound vocal and expressive. This bridges technical exercise with musical application.

patternNote.text: Scale: A Minor Pentatonic with legato connections

notation.title: A Minor Pentatonic with Legato Connections

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Focus on musical phrasing and expression. Vary the dynamics and timing slightly to create a vocal quality. Practice in different keys and scale positions.

exercises.title: Cross-String Legato Patterns
exercises.description: Master legato across multiple strings to create longer, more complex musical phrases. This technique is essential for advanced lead guitar playing.

patternNote.text: Challenge: Maintain legato flow while changing strings

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Practice string transitions slowly to maintain the legato connection. Use minimal picking - only when necessary to move to a new string or restart a phrase.

exercises.title: Slides Combined with Legato
exercises.description: Combine slides with hammer-ons and pull-offs to create extremely expressive and vocal-like passages. This technique is essential for blues and rock lead guitar.

patternNote.text: Technique: Smooth slides connecting legato phrases

notation.title: Expressive Slides Combined with Hammer-Ons and Pull-Offs

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Control the speed of your slides to match the musical context. Slow slides are more expressive, while quick slides add energy. Combine with vibrato for maximum effect.

exercises.title: High-Speed Legato Runs
exercises.description: Develop lightning-fast legato runs for impressive lead guitar solos. This technique allows for incredible speed with minimal pick attacks, creating fluid cascades of notes.

patternNote.text: Goal: Maximum speed with crystal clear note definition

notation.title: Extended Legato Runs for Speed Development

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Build speed gradually and always maintain clarity. Each note must be audible and in time. Use this technique sparingly in musical contexts for maximum impact.

items.title: Technical Development
items: Start with basic two-note hammer-ons and pull-offs
Practice on all strings to develop consistent technique
Focus on volume consistency between picked and hammered notes
Build finger strength gradually with longer patterns
Practice both ascending and descending patterns

challenges.title: Weak Hammered Notes
challenges.text: Strike the fret more decisively with your fingertip. Practice hammer-ons without picking the first note to isolate the technique.

challenges.title: Inconsistent Pull-Offs
challenges.text: Ensure the lower finger is properly positioned before the pull-off. Practice the pulling motion slowly to develop control.

challenges.title: Finger Fatigue
challenges.text: Build stamina gradually with short practice sessions. Rest between exercises and stretch your hands regularly.
